[MUQATIL:20:94-97/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Aaron is the speaker, addressing Moses as his mother’s son.
[MUQATIL:20:94-97/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Aaron explains that if he had objected, the Israelites would have split into factions and killed one another.
[MUQATIL:20:94-97/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Aaron feared Moses would accuse him of dividing Israel and disregarding the instruction to succeed him and set things right (7:142). | mentions 7:142
[MUQATIL:20:94-97/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | reports | Aaron was more beloved to the Israelites than Moses; out of love for Aaron, they named seventy thousand of their children after him.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Light أن in contexts of certainty takes an indicative clause, as if it were heavy أنه; the knowledge statement in 73:20 illustrates this. | mentions 73:20
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The optative أما أن جزاك الله خيرا is allowed without قد or س because it is a prayer; common omission also supports أما إن جزاك الله خيرا.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ما علمت إلا أن تقوم can suggest action without asserting it; a certain future is expressed as ما علمت إلا أن ستقومون.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Light أن is acceptable before a nominal predicate, as in قد علمت أن عمرو ذاهب, because that could also follow heavy أن.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The light أن in أفلا يرون أن لا يرجع إليهم قولا is also followed by an indicative because the clause expresses an asserted fact. | mentions 20:89
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب, أن لا يقدرون is indicative; Abī's codex reportedly reads أنهم لا يقدرون, supporting the heavy-clause analysis. | mentions 57:29
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The أن that governs subjunctive verbs does not occur in a context of certainty and assertion.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After كتبت إليه أن لا, jussive marks a command, subjunctive marks purpose, and indicative reports that the addressee does not do it.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Verbs of supposition ظننت، حسبت، خلت, and رأيت allow either light أن with subjunctive or heavy أن with indicative.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | خشيت normally takes subjunctive because it does not assert an event as established, unlike supposition verbs; the same applies to أرجو، أطمع, and عسى.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | If خشيت concerns an event already established as certain, indicative is possible, though it is not the usual construction.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | قد علمت أن تفعل and قد علمت أن فعل are weak without a future, perfect, or negation marker; these compensate for dropped أنه.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهألفاوكانعلىخمسةأحرف)#565/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A five-letter noun ending in alif deletes that alif in nisba: حبارى becomes حباري, as do جمادى and قرقرى.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهألفاوكانعلىخمسةأحرف)#565/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | rejects | Sībawayh challenges Yunus because his analysis predicts عبدوي and would wrongly count a doubled consonant as one for declension.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهألفاوكانعلىخمسةأحرف)#565/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعض العرب | reports | For declinable حراء, some Arabs say حراوي and others preserve the hamza in حراني.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهألفاوكانعلىخمسةأحرف)#565/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yunus treats مرامى as having an added alif and would form مراموي, by analogy with حبلى becoming حبلوي.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهألفاوكانعلىخمسةأحرف)#565/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | rejects | Sībawayh rejects the overextended analogy because it predicts forms such as مقلولوي, whereas speakers say مقلولي.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهألفاوكانعلىخمسةأحرف)#565/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Deletion is good at the fourth position by analogy with extra alifs; at five or more letters it is required, and greater heaviness strengthens the requirement.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهألفاوكانعلىخمسةأحرف)#565/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Mamdūd nouns retain the final hamza in nisba regardless of length or declension because its case-vowel mobility makes it strong.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهألفاوكانعلىخمسةأحرف)#565/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The maqṣūr alif is weak because it takes no case endings, so it is deleted; a quiescent yāʾ can likewise drop, unlike a moving one.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهألفاوكانعلىخمسةأحرف)#565/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The nisba yāʾ compensates for a deleted weak ending; the alif alternates with the nisba yāʾ as hāʾ alternates in الجحاجحة and الجحاجيح.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهألفاوكانعلىخمسةأحرف)#565/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Nisba on عثير or حثيل follows the pattern of حميري.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهألفاوكانعلىخمسةأحرف)#565/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yunus groups مثنى with معزى and معطى as five-letter nouns like مرامى, implying the same deletion behavior.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمتحركةفيالوصلالتيلاتلحقهازيادة#733/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A nominative ending has four pause forms: ishmām, plain silence, rawm (approximating the vowel), or consonant doubling.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمتحركةفيالوصلالتيلاتلحقهازيادة#733/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Ishmām is visible lip-rounding rather than audible sound, so an unseeing listener cannot distinguish it.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمتحركةفيالوصلالتيلاتلحقهازيادة#733/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | A trusted informant heard an Arab say أعطني أبيضه, adding hāʾ to أبيض at pause by analogy with هنه while intending هن.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمتحركةفيالوصلالتيلاتلحقهازيادة#733/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Ishmām distinguishes an ending mobile in connected speech from one always silent; plain pause treats both alike because both are silent there.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمتحركةفيالوصلالتيلاتلحقهازيادة#733/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Rawm and doubling stress that the ending is normally mobile; doubling is strongest because it requires the following consonant to be vocalized.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمتحركةفيالوصلالتيلاتلحقهازيادة#733/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Sībawayh records notation for the forms: a dot for ishmām, khāʾ for plain silence, a line for rawm, and shīn for doubling.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمتحركةفيالوصلالتيلاتلحقهازيادة#733/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Al-Khalil and Abū al-Khaṭṭāb report Arab rawm; al-Khalil also reports pause without ishmām and with plain silence.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمتحركةفيالوصلالتيلاتلحقهازيادة#733/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Poets add yāʾ, wāw, or alif in rhyme to reflect doubling at pause; examples include سبسبا and عيهل.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمتحركةفيالوصلالتيلاتلحقهازيادة#733/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Ruʾba's rhyme جدبا represents جدب, and his الأضخما represents الأضخم, illustrating added alif in the poetic rhyme practice.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمتحركةفيالوصلالتيلاتلحقهازيادة#733/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | They do not double when the penultimate consonant is already silent, as in عمرو and زيد; rawm or ishmām may still distinguish the ending.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمتحركةفيالوصلالتيلاتلحقهازيادة#733/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In accusative and genitive forms speakers use rawm, doubling, or plain silence, but not ishmām, which depends on the nominative ḍamma.

[SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةاللهذاهبةPageV01P069|فمنذلك#42/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Omitting the object pronoun in عارفه is preferable to rearrangement; speakers often omit this hāʾ, unlike the rare inversion.
[SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةاللهذاهبةPageV01P069|فمنذلك#42/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In وليس كل النوى تلقى المساكين, كل is accusative under تلقى with an implicit subject after ليس; if governed by ليس it would be nominative.
[SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةاللهذاهبةPageV01P069|فمنذلك#42/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The line إذا مت كان الناس صنفان also contains an omitted pronoun, an instance of the same construction.
[SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةاللهذاهبةPageV01P069|فمنذلك#42/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعضهم | reports | Some say كان أنت حير منه, construing it as if an initial إنه preceded أنت.
[SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةاللهذاهبةPageV01P069|فمنذلك#42/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The near-verb كاد allows the same ellipsis: كاد تزيغ means كادت قلوب فريق منهم تزيغ. | mentions 9:117

[SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستفهامفيكونذابمنزلةالذي#460/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Alternatively, ما and ذا form one interrogative noun; ماذا رأيت can be answered خيرا, understood as ما رأيت خير, with accusative matching the question.
[SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستفهامفيكونذابمنزلةالذي#460/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The Qur'anic answer خيرا and idiom عماذا تسأل show that ما وذا can form one interrogative name; otherwise Arabs would say عم ذا تسأل. | mentions 16:30
[SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستفهامفيكونذابمنزلةالذي#460/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | This fused analysis resembles combinations such as إنما، كأنما, and حينما, where elements behave as one expression.
[SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستفهامفيكونذابمنزلةالذي#460/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The Qur'anic response أساطير الأولين is accusative under the fused analysis; a strict relative analysis would call for nominative خير. | mentions 16:24
[SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستفهامفيكونذابمنزلةالذي#460/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The reported line دعى ماذا علمت shows that the relative reading cannot simply be imposed wherever ماذا occurs.
[SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستفهامفيكونذابمنزلةالذي#460/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Short answers like صالح to كيف أصبحت and زيد to من رأيت are understood through an omitted clause; an understood verb can also license accusative after من الذي رأيت.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p273/r7] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | On returning and seeing the calf worship, Moses challenged Aaron and addressed him as his mother's son.

[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p119/r8] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | جلل can describe either great or small: each is large beside something smaller and small beside something larger.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · الحطيئة | reports | Al-Ḥuṭayʾa reverses the syntax: the hoof holds the rope, rather than the rope holding the hoof; each holds the other while attached.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r2] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · الأخطل | reports | Al-Akhṭal reverses the roles; the intended sense is that the group’s backsides reached Najrān and Hajar, since what one reaches also reaches one.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r3] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · آخر | reports | An anonymous poet puts الأفعوان and الشجاع in the accusative where the expected construction makes them nominative, since allies act on one another.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r4] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · الشماخ | reports | Al-Shammākh reverses agent and object in عصب العلباء بالعود; the expected order is عصب العود بالعلباء, though either construction is used.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r5] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · ذو الرمة | reports | Dhū al-Rummah reverses object and recipient: he means clothing the waist with a shield, since كسوت can take the garment or its wearer as object.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r6] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · أبو النجم | reports | Abū al-Najm reverses what approaches what: he means the constellation approaching the horizon, since each draws near to the other.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r7] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · الراعي | reports | Al-Rāʿī says hunters see the eye as a track, where the expected phrasing is that they see the track as clearly as an eye; the inversion is reciprocal.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r8] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · النابغة | reports | Al-Nābigha reverses the comparison of fears; he means the antelope’s fear is no greater than his own, so their fears are equal.

[NAHHAS:v3p54/r22] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | reports | Aaron asks Moses not to seize his beard or head because the people might mistake it for contempt or punishment; another report says Moses did not act from either motive.
